svg.text: How far can the optical reference of public IMU datasets be trusted?
The 21 errors we have worked through so far in 18 public datasets with IMUs and optical motion capture, in the order we detect and correct them

Each check runs only after every error that would distort its estimate. Detection is implemented for every error shown; the badge says what happens to the data. All numbers are exploratory readings, status 2026-11-10.
What happens to the data

flagged; cannot be corrected

svg.text: Why this order
Reference-only checks first.
Nearly every later check compares IMU and reference; these depend on no other error.
Sample defects next.
A single bad sample shifts every later estimate; clipping before stuck channels, so a channel pinned at its limit is not counted twice.
Assignment before time.
An offset measured against the wrong recording means nothing.
Gyroscope offset, then mounting, then gravity.
The offset comes from rest, which needs no mounting; the mounting fit uses the corrected gyroscope; the accelerometer checks need the sensor
turned into the segment.
Timing errors: detected one by one, corrected together.
Recommended, not yet decided: align the IMU time scales, then remove the shared drift, then the offset, as one straight-line time correction per IMU.
Main readings so far (exploratory)
Timing is the most common error.
Time offset in 16 of 18 datasets; clock drift in 8 of the 14 datasets with trials of at least 60 s.
Its correction gains mostly less than 1°,
visible only where the rest of the data is clean (DIODEM, dfjimu, Hankyong); elsewhere larger, still uncorrected errors dominate.
Assignment errors are rare but large.
Each stream is real motion, so wrongly paired trials give plausible and wrong joint angles.
Sample defects are few.
They barely move the joint-angle error, but would distort every later fit.

Error numbers follow the agreed order of detection and correction: each check runs on data corrected for every error with a smaller number. Effect: change of the MEKF joint-angle error after the correction.
